content:
ashwin: Heads-up: fenris12b int4 canary started showing intermittent OOMs under >120 token bursts. Started ~2h after quant rollout. Pattern looks like KV cache growth + memory slot fragmentation.

liz: Ugh, do we have a quick repro or logs?

ashwin: Pasting a trimmed log snippet from the failing worker: 

```
2026-03-20T18:03:12Z ERROR inference: allocation failed: cudaMemAlloc OOM
model=fenris12b variant=int4 host=gpu-31
stack: serving/runtime/kv_cache.cpp:line 214
kv_cache_size=3.8GB session_slots=48 active_sessions=42
max_new_tokens=256 batch=8
```

ashwin: Also seeing memmap churn in /sys/kernel/mm/.. - fragmentation spikes after ~30mins of traffic.

carmen: Important bits: batch=8 + max_new_tokens=256 on int4 + prefetch enabled is a risky combo. Prefetch inflates transient working set.

nora: Did quant rollout alter kernel selection? int4 sometimes chooses less memory-friendly attention kernel.

ashwin: Yes, kernel profile changed to use bernoulli-slim attention path for speed. Might be using a larger temp buffer for certain seq lengths.

liz: Quick mitigation options: 
- drop default max_new_tokens to 128 for fenris12b canary route
- set batching.max_batch_size=4 for this model 
- toggle prefetch=false for canary instances 
- enable session_cache_ttl=30s to purge idle KV shards sooner

carmen: Add to that: enable slowstart microbatching: `microbatch.starting_batch=1 duration=45s` so warmups don't allocate big contiguous pages at once. Also reduce kv_eviction_threshold from 0.6 -> 0.4.

nora: Sounds reasonable. We should run a regression eval before we roll changes to hosted. Lowering max_new_tokens may affect some QA prompts. I'll run the eval suite (quick-quality and longform) on the canary after config changes.

ashwin: I ran a quick local perf run: with `max_new_tokens=128, batch=4, prefetch=false` peak mem for a 160-token request dropped from 4.1GB -> 2.6GB and no OOMs in 30 iterations. Quality delta looks tiny on a few smoke prompts.

carmen: One code note: there's a race where `session_state` isn't freed until full GC cycle; I can push a tiny runtime patch to aggressively free zero-ref KV shards on checkpoint boundaries. Low-risk.

liz: Plan then: 
1) Apply runtime patch (carmen) to free inactive KV shards (canary only) 
2) Update canary config: max_new_tokens=128, max_batch_size=4, prefetch=false, session_cache_ttl=30s, microbatch.starting_batch=1 duration=45s (ashwin will roll) 
3) Run quick-quality eval (nora) on canary 1h after roll 
4) If no regressions and OOMs gone -> gradually bump canary traffic and re-run full eval suite before wider roll.

ashwin: I'll start the config roll now on the fenris12b-canary pool and attach the deploy diff here.

deploy-bot: deploy 4968012345-config-rollout started for pool=fenris-fenris12b-canary by ashwin at 2026-03-20T18:14:02Z.

ashwin: deploy diff: 
```
models.fenris12b.canary:
  max_new_tokens: 128
  batching:
    max_batch_size: 4
  prefetch: false
  session_cache_ttl_seconds: 30
  microbatch:
    starting_batch: 1
    duration_seconds: 45
kv.eviction_threshold: 0.4
```

carmen: I'll prep the runtime patch and open a PR now. Small unit tests included.

nora: Kicked off quick-quality eval job: job id eval-496801 and linked prompts. If we see >2% regression on longform F1 we rollback.

liz: Also add a temporary alert in Console: `fenris12b.canary.oom_rate > 0` to mute noisy platform-wide alerts while we iterate.

ashwin: Current status: config rolled, canary running, watch window 30m. I'll post metrics in 10m.

nora: If the runtime patch lands before end of watch window we can enable it for canary immediately. Otherwise patch after watch.

ashwin: 10m checkpoint: OOMs stopped, fragmentation metric trending down. eval-496801 quick-quality shows negligible quality delta on 200 prompts.

carmen: PR #4829 opened: `runtime: aggressive-kv-free-on-checkpoint` - small, canary-only flag `kv_aggressive_free=true`.

ashwin: Approving and enabling on canary now.

deploy-bot: feature flag `kv_aggressive_free` enabled for pool fenris-fenris12b-canary by ashwin.

liz: Excellent. Next steps: keep canary at 5% traffic and run full eval suite overnight. If stable, we can propose new defaults for fenris12b in model catalog (max_new_tokens=128, default_batch_cap=4, prefetch default off).

nora: I'll summarize evaluation results and open a roll proposal if all green.

ashwin: Thanks all. Filed follow-up ticket INF-2147 to revisit kernel selection heuristics for int4 attention buffers.

carmen: Nice work. :thumbsup:

liz: :eyes: good iteration pace.

ashwin: tagging this thread done-after-roll; will close once full-eval passes or we rollback.
